name: std::async future-handling pattern (store futures, collect later)
listed_description: Book times 32 std::async tasks of 10 ms each and shows that discarding or immediately destroying each future serializes the tasks, while launching all tasks first and storing futures in a vector overlaps them.
claim_text: Discarded or in-place futures take 334 ms, reusing one future 166 ms, storing futures in a vector then calling get 22 ms.
book_benchmark: 32 std::async(std::launch::async) tasks, each sleeping 10 ms, timed with std::chrono high_resolution_clock; compiler and flags not stated; CPU stated as i7 4790K at 4 GHz, four cores and eight threads. Baseline is the same tasks with each future destroyed at once (about 334 ms). Companion code expected under Chapter_07; file list not confirmed.
guessed_baseline: std::async with the returned future destroyed (joined) inside the launch loop
found_in: book: Asynchronous Programming with C++ (2024), ch. 7, section Async futures and performance

name: cppcoro
listed_description: Library of C++ coroutine abstractions (task, generator, awaitable primitives, thread pool) that the book names as a helper for the low-level C++20 coroutine support.
guessed_baseline: std::future/std::async or hand-written coroutine promise types
found_in: book: Asynchronous Programming with C++ (2024), ch. 8, section on writing a first coroutine

name: uberlog
listed_description: Cross-platform, multi-process C++ logging system. Book table credits it for multi-process and distributed use and says it is not as fast as specialized low-latency loggers.
claim_text: Book says only: not as fast as specialized low-latency loggers. Repo README (not the book) claims about 200 ns per message on Windows and 280 ns on Linux, author-measured.
found_in: book: Asynchronous Programming with C++ (2024), ch. 11, section Some relevant logging libraries and Table 11.1

name: Easylogging++
listed_description: Single-header C++ logging library with custom sinks and performance tracking. Book table says it is less performance-optimized than some other libraries. Repo is archived read-only since July 2025.
claim_text: Book says only: less performance-optimized than some other libraries. README (not the book) claims extremely fast, qualitative only, no numbers.
found_in: book: Asynchronous Programming with C++ (2024), ch. 11, section Some relevant logging libraries and Table 11.1
